deposits.notes:
Verified public, without credentials, on 2026-10-09. The repository is named both in the PDF and in both URLs in forms/c419.json data_and_code; recorded once with found_by=paper. The repository web URL and recursive GitHub tree API both returned HTTP 200. API: https://api.github.com/repos/mcneural-lab/sft-cognitive-synergies/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1. The non-truncated tree contains 114 blob files; files lists 50 selected entries, prioritizing the study data and relevant analysis code. Snapshot commit: 8c7656b06f246dd01a71d3e149b162021b9756ab. Individual files were read from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcneural-lab/sft-cognitive-synergies/8c7656b06f246dd01a71d3e149b162021b9756ab/<path>, all inspected files returning HTTP 200.

rows_checked=4810 refers specifically to data/dyadic/conceptnet/ai_words_processed.csv, not to people or the total across files. columns_checked is the union of column names read across the inspected CSV and embedding files, not a single shared schema.

S4: ai_words_processed.csv has 4810 word rows: 2435 source=user human words and 2375 source=ai words, with 144 distinct playerID values. dyadType=AI and prompt identifies adjacent (convergent; 48 people), divergent (46), or inferred (50). It includes category, roundIndex, gameID, playerID, text, original_text, normalized_text, irt, relativeTimestamp, word_index, switch, label, snafu_cat, and switch_snafu. has_arm_assignment=true means the received condition is identifiable, not that random allocation is established.

S4: hh_words_processed.csv has 3345 word rows, 96 gameID values, and 192 distinct source identifiers, exactly two sources per game. Its playerID column has only 96 distinct values and must not be used alone to count all human participants. Use source for the person who generated each human-human word; map AI-file source=user to that row's playerID. The intersection of HH source and AI playerID is 129 people, with paired prompt counts adjacent/convergent=45, divergent=36, inferred=48, matching PDF p. 71, Figure S12. Retain gameID to account for dependence within human-human pairs and participant IDs to account for repeated measures.

S1/S3 pooled solo data: solo_words_processed.csv has 6877 word rows from 121 distinct playerID values and 190 person-category sequences (animals=61, clothes=64, supermarket=65). These are retained observations; 190 is not a count of distinct people. The paper identifies this pool as Experiments 1 and 3; a direct mapping of each retained participant to the original experiment was not confirmed.

All three precomputed ConceptNet embedding files were also downloaded and inspected in memory using a restricted pandas/numpy unpickler: ai_words_with_embeddings_switches.pkl has 4810 rows (13720555 bytes), hh_words_with_embeddings_switches.pkl 3345 rows (9552101 bytes), and solo_words_with_embeddings_switches.pkl 6877 rows (19376836 bytes). Each contains 300-dimensional embedding arrays, text_unmodified, column-sequence-id, switch_sim, and switch_method=median in addition to its corresponding CSV columns. These are companion representations of the same outputs, not additional participants. The README explains that pickle text is transformed for embedding lookup while text_unmodified preserves the CSV text.

S2: data/final/filtered/all_human_wordpreds_unique_filtered.csv has 6269 rows and columns gameID_pred, id, response, irt, source_id, rank, normalizedPredicted, data-category, model, type. There are 174 distinct id and 174 non-null distinct gameID_pred values; source_id has 172 distinct values and denotes the source sequence, not the predictor. Some predictions and gameID_pred cells are missing, so apply the supplied analysis rules. The three results/micro/prediction/next-exemplar/gemini-3.0-pro CSVs have animals=2141, clothes=1765, and supermarket=2170 rows, with 58 assignment IDs in each category. Columns include id, rank, model, category, input_sequence, actual_response, predicted_response, normalizedPredicted, is_correct, and is_human_correct. They support per-assignment human and AI prediction-accuracy summaries.

S3: results/micro/prediction/switch/gemini-3.0-pro files have animals=2313 rows/62 IDs, clothes=1799 rows/59 IDs, and supermarket=2308 rows/60 IDs. Columns include id, rank, category, input_sequence, actual_response, predicted_switch_response, human_switch_prediction, embedding_switch_prediction, and switch_embedding. These are session/sequence-assignment IDs, not a confirmed study-wide unique-person count. Ten animal rows lack a human switch prediction. Do not use the generic is_correct field for switch accuracy: it was uniformly false in the inspected animal file. The supplied switch-analysis code explicitly uses embedding_switch_prediction as ground truth and compares it with human_switch_prediction or predicted_switch_response.

S5: data/sequences/human/hills/hills.csv was read in memory: 5220 rows, 141 distinct IDs, with columns id, response, irt, source, trial, unfiltered_response, category, cumirt, rank, switch, split, data-category. This confirms the 141-sequence archival benchmark subset; it does not independently verify all of the 699-sequence analyses. The 80969252-byte logit-lens archive exceeds the 20 MB inspection limit and was not downloaded. S6 pilot membership and S7 simulation coverage were not confirmed.

has_outcome_scores=true is supported by recorded response times, switch indicators, prediction outcomes, and their underlying words/embeddings. S4 concept counts, self/other cosine similarities, late-minus-early summaries, and partner midpoint similarity are derived from these word-level records rather than supplied as a ready-made participant summary table. src/sftbench/dyadic/load_data.py and word_count.py were read, not executed; they document source mapping, adjacent-to-convergent recoding, category selection, embedding alignment, similarity calculation, and paired aggregation.

Reanalysis can compute S4-O1 human concept counts per person, S4-O3 counts per dyad, arm means/SDs/SEs, eligible analyzed counts, and paired differences; S4-O2/S4-O4/S4-O5 similarity outcomes can be reconstructed from the provided embeddings and ordered, attributed words. Texts also permit within-person lexical/semantic diversity and between-person overlap or homogenization analyses. S2-O1 prediction accuracy and S3 session-level switch accuracy can be summarized from trial records. Analysis must respect participant/dyad dependence, the processed-data inclusion rules, missing observations, and category/condition matching. The deposit does not establish the initial randomized enrollment count, recover excluded participants, or establish random assignment of AI assistance.

LICENSE and LICENSE-DATA were read: code is MIT; bundled data/ and results/ are CC BY-SA 4.0, with third-party source attributions. The README identifies this work as PNAS in press but provides no journal article DOI. No remote code was executed, and no downloaded data or code was saved to disk.

notes:
The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through its end, including all supplementary material (77 PDF pages). The saved source is arXiv:2608.26152v2; its landing page confirms the 28 August 2026 revision. Key quotations were extracted directly from the local PDF with PyMuPDF; line breaks are preserved where they occur. No preregistration, separate supplement deposit, embargo, or on-request data statement was found.

forms/c419.json contains no final field or final.open_items; open_questions is an empty list. Therefore what_we_could_compute is null specifically for the requested mapping to final.open_items. This is not an absence of computable data: the outcome-specific reanalysis opportunities are documented in the deposit notes.

S4 received partner and prompt conditions are recoverable. The PDF/form do not confirm random assignment of AI prompt or partner order, and the repository's condition labels do not resolve that design question. Random assignment in S2/S3 refers to sequence stimuli, not human access to AI. Public data availability is established independently of screening eligibility.

Public data and embedding contents, condition labels, participant links, row counts, and licensing were directly inspected. The data checks reproduce the principal retained and paired S4 counts printed in the PDF. Each downloaded data file was below 20 MB and read only in memory. Only this requested JSON file was written.

Title and first-author searches used only the named APIs, with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier. Successful API searches were HTTP 200; identical repeated checks are consolidated. Search results did not reveal an additional relevant data deposit. DataCite's relevant hit is the manuscript DOI, not a second dataset. The OSF API's title-only search is less comprehensive than a contributor search; the DataCite author-field query supplements it.

The supplied publisher/preprint landing pages https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26152 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26152v2 both returned HTTP 200. Their supplementary-file review found the paper PDF/HTML/TeX links but no separate ancillary participant-data link or journal DOI. The manuscript includes Supplementary Information; generic arXiv Code/Data/Media toggles are not identified deposits. The GitHub README calls the paper PNAS in press; no PNAS landing URL was supplied or confirmed.

All explicit external hyperlinks found in the PDF/markdown and the form's duplicate data/code URLs were checked. Link results: https://github.com/mcneural-lab/sft-cognitive-synergies/tree/main -> HTTP 200; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1111/1467-9450.00248 -> HTTP 403 (bot-check page; stopped without attempting access); https://humansand.ai/ -> HTTP 200; https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/interaction-models/ -> HTTP 200; https://www.together.ai -> HTTP 200; http://github.com/unslothai/unsloth -> HTTP 200 (redirected to https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth); https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.26152 -> HTTP 200 (redirected to https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26152).
